newsitem.title: USA: Arco says considers disposal of coal assets.
newsitem.headline: Arco says considers disposal of coal assets.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. said Tuesday it was likely to withdraw from the coal business through the spin-off of its U.S. coal operations and a sale or public offering of its Australian operations.
Los Angeles-based Arco's U.S. coal mining operations, the nation's fourth-largest, will be formed into a stand alone company and possibly spun-off to shareholders.
"At this point there are no buyers being solicited," Arco spokesman Albert Greenstein said, adding an advisory committee was being formed to decide a course of action.
Arco's coal assets were valued at $1.75 billion at the end of 1996, out of assets totalling of $25.7 billion, he said. Net income from coal operations for 1996 was $60 million.
Arco Coal Co. employment at year-end 1996 was 2,600, including about 1,000 in Australia.
Arco's domestic mining operations are located in Wyoming, Colorado and Utah.
"While Arco has some of the best coal assets in the world, we no longer regard them as part of our core business," Arco Chairman Mike Bowlin said in a statement.
Arco also said it will likely to sell its Australian coal interests outright or hold a public offering.
The overall process is expected to take at least six months and could extend into 1998.
